task.title: Beads migration inspection truncates >1 MiB native history and misreports ENOBUFS as source evidence failure
task.description:
## Impact and evidence

Read-only Beads → Backlog migration inspection in Ralph PVA is blocked by command-output capture, not demonstrated source corruption. Joe assigned this Conversation ticket creation only. The reporting session verified the reproduction on 2026-10-31; this Conversation read its complete handoff and confirmed the corresponding tracked code, but did not rerun Beads or inspect the private history payload.

In `/Users/jlanders/gitlab_local/ralph-pva`, `initialize_prime_claw(action="switch-request", targetProvider="backlog")` returned `status=blocked`, `code=preflight`. Detail began `bd history playwrite_testing-x9ro.11: [` and ended mid-JSON, with generic advice to repair native source/publication evidence. The historical Slack-repair description is task data, not migration-repair instructions.

The reporter captured the source successfully with:

```text
bd --readonly history playwrite_testing-x9ro.11 --json --limit 0 > /tmp/ralph-pva-history-preflight-20261031/playwrite_testing-x9ro.11-history.json 2> /tmp/ralph-pva-history-preflight-20261031/history.stderr
```

Result: exit 0, empty stderr, 1,305,475 bytes, valid JSON array with 108 records, every `Issue.id` equal to `playwrite_testing-x9ro.11`.

Using the saved file (not another Beads invocation), the reporter reproduced the installed capture options:

```javascript
execFileSync('/bin/cat', [historyFile], {
  encoding: 'utf8', stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
})
```

Caught metadata: `code=ENOBUFS`, `status=null`, `signal=SIGTERM`, message `spawnSync /bin/cat ENOBUFS`, stdout 1,114,112 bytes, stderr 0 bytes. Original preflight detail was 1,114,150 UTF-8 bytes, consistent with its label plus the truncated stdout. This proves a command-capture limit; it does not prove malformed native history.

## Cause and affected source

Installed diagnostic locations were `~/.prime/agent/extension-support/project-initialization.ts` lines 140–157 and `task-provider-migration.ts`. They are evidence, not an authorized patch target. Corresponding builder source at main `500b386002badc4af9824b8a2e85752f35c5e3f3`:

- `src/prime-agent-plugin/extension-support/project-initialization.ts:140–157`, `ProcessCommandRunner.run`: `execFileSync` has no explicit `maxBuffer`. The catch uses `String(error?.stderr ?? error?.message ?? error)`, so empty stderr masks the useful message; null status becomes 1 and code/signal are lost.
- `src/prime-agent-plugin/extension-support/task-provider-migration.ts:589–590`, `captureBeads`: reads full per-task native history and events with `--limit 0`.
- The same file at line 236, `commandFailure`: prefers trimmed stderr, then stdout, then exit status. It therefore exposes a large truncated historical payload instead of the output-limit cause.

## Required outcome

Capture complete output for all native Beads source reads used by migration, including export, inventory, task views, history, events and provenance, without a fixed per-command size ceiling, subject to available resources, without truncation or silent omission. Merely raising a fixed output-buffer cap is not sufficient. Resource failures must remain explicit and fail safely with source authority intact; this is not a promise of unlimited memory or storage. Preserve all existing tasks, history, configuration and provenance. Per-task full in-memory output capture is an implementation choice, not a universal migration requirement. Choose the smallest sound repair; this specification does not prescribe a new architecture or an implementation plan.

Distinguish command transport/output-limit failures from malformed or incomplete native data. Diagnostics must be bounded and actionable: identify the failed command and available error code/status/signal. A short bounded excerpt of native stderr is permitted to explain ordinary failures; captured stdout and native task/history payloads must never be included. Do not substitute stdout when stderr is empty. Empty stderr and null status must not erase ENOBUFS. Do not recommend trimming history, changing task statuses, or repairing otherwise readable source data to work around this transport bug.

## Preservation and safety boundaries

Source authority must remain intact whenever complete capture cannot be proven. Preserve stable source identity/revision, complete inventory/history/provenance, quiescence, active ownership continuity, destination verification/publication, receipt and cutover/deletion protections. Do not add outgoing source-publication requirements or unused lifecycle statuses merely to read retiring data. Do not invent an extra preservation-approval gate.

Ralph initialization is complete; migration has NOT run. No `switch-confirm`, source repair/retirement, or successfully inspected exact source revision exists for this attempt. Prior inventory (406 issues: 349 closed, 42 open, 10 in_progress, 5 blocked) is historical, not fresh completeness evidence. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is stale and non-authoritative. Prior setup/report checkpoints `094cbb7` and `4a31c26` are not claims about current HEAD.

Preserve existing Backlog RPVA-1, RPVA-2, and the distinct archived RPVA-2 prefix probe, plus configuration parked at `backlog/config.yml.pre-migration` by `3f29fb6`. Do not restore, reset, renumber, or discard them. Intended destination remains independent `.backlog/` with the root native configuration symlink and consolidation of existing records/config/history. Preserve mappings: legacy open → In Design; ordinary closed → Done/completed, not automatic archive; retain raw status, close reasons and relationships.

PRIMECLAW-46's outgoing-status defect was consolidated into PRIMECLAW-44; Joe reported it cleared. PRIMECLAW-49 concerns native memory records. This is a distinct subsequent output-buffer failure, not either source-schema defect.

Ticket creation authorizes no implementation, live Ralph command/retry/migration, store/config mutation, global installation, Prime Agent patch, merge or cleanup. Future candidate work must use synthetic disposable fixtures and Docker-only plugin validation. Actual cutover still needs exact revision/counts/ownership, semantic placement, a bounded maintenance window, quiesced writers and explicit one-way migration/source-deletion confirmation. Do not paste private history or bulk-read the reporter's log; the metadata and synthetic reproduction are sufficient.

nodes.title: Beads migration inspection truncates >1 MiB native history and misreports ENOBUFS as source evidence failure

acceptanceCriteria.text: Complete output capture for all native Beads source reads used by migration (including export, inventory, task views, history, events and provenance) has no fixed per-command size ceiling, subject to available resources, and never truncates or silently omits data; merely raising a fixed buffer cap is insufficient. A synthetic case representing the reported 1,305,475-byte, 108-record history verifies complete retention; resource failure remains explicit and safe.

Output-limit/transport failures remain distinct from invalid JSON or incomplete native data; ENOBUFS is identifiable even with empty stderr and null status, with available command/code/status/signal metadata retained.

Failure diagnostics have a bounded size and display command/error metadata with an optional short bounded native stderr excerpt, but never captured stdout or native task/history payloads, including when stderr is empty. They do not advise repairing readable source data for a command-capture failure; ordinary command errors remain actionable.

When complete capture is not proven, inspection fails safely without destination writes or source mutation/retirement; existing preservation, identity, stable capture, quiescence, ownership, publication, receipt and explicit cutover/deletion safeguards remain intact.

Disposable synthetic Docker regression coverage exercises >1 MiB valid history/events, ENOBUFS with empty stderr/null status, ordinary command errors and genuinely malformed native JSON, without live Ralph access or global plugin changes.

task.implementationPlan:
## Implementation approach

Keep the existing synchronous `CommandRunner.run` and native snapshot/package flow. Replace fixed pipe-buffer capture with private temporary-file/file-descriptor capture for migration commands; successful results still return complete strings for the existing parsers. This removes the per-command capture ceiling without an async migration rewrite. Memory/string and temporary-storage exhaustion remain resource failures, not a promise of unlimited capacity. Do not add a migration framework, persistent spool registry, retry loop, new state machine, or preservation-approval gate. Do not implement deterministic machinery for task reconciliation, iterative plan changes, or semantic judgments that the Episode or Conversation can perform. Semantic decisions stay with the Conversation/Episode.

1. **Repair capture at the existing runner seam.** In `extension-support/project-initialization.ts`, implement file-backed capture with one small helper at the existing runner seam. Do not add a parallel runner framework, runner registry, command-routing framework, or configurable capture-policy system. Redirect child stdout and stderr to private files rather than `execFileSync` pipes, wait for completion, and read complete successful stdout. Keep other runner consumers compatible and avoid changing unrelated command behavior. Wire both `inspectTaskProviderMigration` and `migrateTaskProvider` in `extension-support/task-provider-migration.ts` to use this path throughout source capture and recapture, including export, independent inventory, task views, histories, events, provenance and identity/version/catalog reads. Close descriptors and remove only this invocation's temporary files in `finally`, on success and failure. File creation, child execution and output-read failures must fail closed; never parse or certify a partial captured result. No fixed `maxBuffer` increase, output clipping, history pagination/omission, or source-data workaround.

2. **Preserve failure metadata and render safe diagnostics.** Extend the runner result with backward-compatible optional native error code, original nullable exit status and signal (retain the existing numeric status convention for callers). Preserve these values for spawn/capture/resource failures and nonzero exits; empty stderr must not hide `ENOBUFS`. In migration `runRequired`/`commandFailure`, distinguish command/capture failure (including resource failure) from invalid native data using the existing failure paths, preserved metadata and simple diagnostic formatting. Do not build a generalized error taxonomy or classification framework. Use a bounded safe command label and available metadata plus an optional short bounded stderr excerpt; never fall back to captured stdout, dump an error's output/cause object, or print payload-bearing command arguments. Bound the complete rendered diagnostic, not just stderr. Make migration JSON parse errors identify the command/data kind without echoing input or raw parser messages that can quote private history. Update inspection/migration error advice so command transport/resource failures advise resolving that failure, not repairing readable source data; genuinely invalid/incomplete native data remains a distinct actionable failure.

3. **Add focused synthetic Docker regressions.** Extend `tests/task_provider_migration.test.mjs` and, where needed, `tests/project_initialization_extension.test.mjs` through their existing Docker pytest bridges; do not create a new test harness. Exercise the production capture runner, not only fake string-returning runners: generate valid 108-record history representing the reported 1,305,475-byte case, retain a tail sentinel, and compare full output/record content. Cover large history and events with reusable synthetic data, and use small shared-path/routing assertions to prove that export, inventory, show and provenance use the same uncapped path. Reuse existing migration fixtures for lossless destination retention. Do not generate 108 real Beads revisions, build separate integration fixtures for every command/error combination, or expand this into a duplicated test matrix. Add a larger-than-baseline case and multibyte content to catch incorrect byte handling. Finite stress tests are not proof of no fixed ceiling: also review source capture for finite pipe-buffer limits or byte cutoffs. Existing fixture helpers use capped `execFileSync`; oversized fixture reads/assertions must use the repaired production path or known fixture bytes instead. Inject `ENOBUFS` with empty stderr/null native status and signal, ordinary nonzero command failures with short/oversized/empty stderr, and temporary-storage/output-read resource failures; assert bounded actionable metadata, private stdout/tail sentinels absent from diagnostics, cleanup on handled success/failure, and no destination writes or source/ownership mutation when initial capture fails. A real malformed native JSON case must fail as invalid data without exposing its payload. Keep existing migration preservation, stable recapture, exact revision/inventory, ownership continuity, receipt, publication and cutover/deletion tests intact.

4. **Validate and document only this repair.** Update `docs/project-initialization.md` to explain complete migration capture subject to available resources, private temporary-file cleanup, and bounded transport-versus-data diagnostics. Run the focused Docker suites and required tier-1 probe after plugin-source changes; record results in this task's native Implementation Notes:
   - `python3 -m pytest tests/test_task_provider_migration.py::test_task_provider_migration_node_suite tests/test_project_initialization.py::test_project_initialization_node_suite tests/test_beads_retiring_source_capture.py -q -m container`
   - `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe`
   - Before candidate review, `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -m container` for shared-runner and lifecycle regression coverage.
   The probe alone does not run migration regressions. Inject resource failures deterministically; do not exhaust real host/container resources. Reuse current native migration fixtures to verify that retained history/events/provenance arrive losslessly in destination packages. Check existing shared-runner behavior if its interface changes. No live Ralph reads/retries/migration, private payload access, Prime Agent edits, user-global apply/check/probes, new lifecycle statuses, outgoing publication requirement, concurrency-gate repair, or automatic migration confirmation. Existing task/config/provenance preservation and explicit one-way cutover authority remain unchanged.

## Execution and review boundary

Implement only after separate operator `/implement-task PRIMECLAW-50` approval. Use disposable synthetic projects and Docker candidate validation. PRIMECLAW-49 covers native memory records independently; do not fold that work or the unrelated hard-coded lifecycle gates into this bug. Recheck the current main baseline at implementation time and preserve compatible upstream changes. Leave source authority intact on every unproven capture. Publish the candidate and task evidence through the normal Episode review flow; global activation and any real source deletion require their own existing operator authority.

task.title: Add agent-callable implement_task entry point for approved tasks
task.description:
## Context and outcome
Prime Claw currently mixes agent-invoked Markdown skills, agent-callable tools, and custom slash commands. Planning has an agent-callable entry point, but implementation starts through `/implement-task`, leaving the operator to supply command syntax even after giving a clear conversational instruction.

Replace Prime Claw's custom slash-command workflow with Markdown skills and commands/tools exposed to the agent. Skills tell the agent how to interpret the operator's request and invoke the supported operations. The operator should be able to direct the workflow conversationally without a required custom slash-command invocation.

This supersedes the original narrow proposal to add only `implement_task`. The inspected custom-command inventory is `/plan`, `/plan-spec`, `/implement-task`, `/implement-spec`, and `/handoff`. Remove Prime Claw's custom registrations, not Prime Agent's built-in commands or its native `/skill:` invocation mechanism.

## Required behavior
Provide discoverable Markdown skill guidance and agent-callable operations for the workflow outcomes currently reached through those commands, including task-native planning and implementation, ordinary handoff, and retained folder-based compatibility where it is currently supported. Reuse existing tools where they already provide the outcome rather than adding redundant interfaces. Add the missing agent-facing implementation entry capability.

Skills must explain how to bind the intended task or retained specification, resolve material ambiguity, invoke the corresponding operation, interpret admission versus completion, and stop or continue appropriately. Users must not need to issue a custom slash command as a prerequisite. Update installed managed guidance and relevant product documentation so they describe the same skills-and-agent-operations interface.

Preserve task/provider identity, lifecycle-state validation, semantic readiness, placement selection, ownership, isolated Episode allocation, and the single fixed execute assignment. Do not let the interface change bypass resource-safety checks or silently broaden approved scope. Preserve supported legacy outcomes without retaining custom slash commands as a hidden required entry path. Failed or uncertain admission or partial creation must not cause automatic duplicate admission or Episode allocation.

## Approval and enforcement boundary
Markdown skills own the workflow rules for advancing between phases. They interpret the operator's approval and decide when to invoke the corresponding operations. An explicit conditional instruction such as "plan this task, then implement it when ready" may authorize that sequence within the approved scope; it does not require fresh approval solely because planning finished. A request to plan alone does not authorize implementation.

Native tools enforce concrete task/provider identity, valid lifecycle state, semantic readiness, placement, ownership, and resource safety. They must not require proof that a particular earlier entry point or invocation sequence was used as a substitute for the skill's interpretation of operator authority. This does not remove readiness or resource-safety validation.

## Delegated task selection and lifecycle readiness
The operator may explicitly delegate selection of work within stated bounds. The skill may select a matching task and must bind its exact canonical identity before invoking task-specific native operations. Delegated task selection is not permission to skip design or planning.

Implementation eligibility is represented by the existing task workflow states: a task must have progressed through design and planning and be in `In Planning` before implementation admission. Selecting a "ready to implement" task therefore means selecting from that eligible lifecycle state, not merely taking the highest-priority open task or relying on dependency readiness alone. Preserve the existing semantic readiness checks; do not add a second phase-history receipt or invocation-sequence proof alongside the task's native lifecycle state.

## Retained folder-based compatibility
Keep the currently supported retained folder-based planning, implementation, and continuation behavior. Replace its custom slash-command entry points with Markdown skill guidance and agent-callable operations. Removing custom commands is not authority to retire retained version-1 workflows, migrate their ownership, delete their plans, or alter their resource lifecycle.

The material operator-interview decisions are resolved. This specification remains `In Design` for operator review. Specification approval permits only the separate planning workflow; it does not itself start planning or implementation.

## Scope boundaries
This work replaces the Prime Claw workflow invocation surface; it does not remove operator authority over product, scope, merge, abandonment, or destructive actions. It does not introduce an orchestrator, new task provider, or an autonomous delivery loop.

Prefer provider-native behavior, then concise LLM instructions for semantic judgment, then only narrow deterministic integrity and transport code. Do not implement deterministic machinery for task reconciliation, iterative plan changes, semantic approval classification, or other reasoning that the Episode or Conversation can perform through the LLM. Do not add persistent state or state machines unless a named acceptance criterion cannot otherwise be met and the implementation plan demonstrates why they are necessary.

Prime Agent remains an upstream dependency. Changes belong in prime-claw's plugin, managed guidance, documentation, and tests. Candidate plugin validation remains Docker-isolated, with no candidate host/user-global apply or probe before acceptance. Installation/cutover behavior must respect the existing full-restart and active-resource safety requirements.

nodes.title: Add agent-callable implement_task entry point for approved tasks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Prime Claw no longer registers its custom /plan, /plan-spec, /implement-task, /implement-spec, or /handoff commands; Prime Agent built-ins and native /skill: invocation are unaffected.

Discoverable Markdown skills instruct the agent how to invoke supported workflow operations, bind exact task or retained-specification identity, resolve material ambiguity, and distinguish admission from completion without requiring custom slash commands. Explicit delegated task selection stays within the operator's bounds; implementation selection requires the existing In Planning lifecycle state after design and planning, not dependency readiness alone, and preserves semantic readiness checks without a separate phase-history proof.

Every supported workflow outcome formerly reached through the removed custom commands remains reachable through agent-callable operations and skill guidance, including implementation entry, task-native planning, ordinary handoff, and retained folder-based planning/implementation/continuation. Existing tools are reused where sufficient. Retained version-1 workflows, ownership, plans, and resource lifecycle are not retired or migrated by this invocation change.

Markdown skills own phase-advancement and approval policy, honor explicit conditional approval for planning followed by implementation within approved scope, and do not infer implementation authority from planning alone. Native tools enforce concrete identity/state/readiness/placement/ownership/resource safety without requiring a particular prior workflow-entry invocation sequence.

The new invocation surface preserves provider/canonical identity, required lifecycle states, readiness checks, placement decisions, ownership, isolated Episode creation, and the one fixed execute assignment, without duplicate admission or allocation after failed or uncertain results.

Managed installed guidance and relevant workflow/user-story documentation consistently describe skills plus agent-callable operations and no longer prescribe removed custom slash commands as required workflow entry points.

Focused automated coverage proves removal of custom registrations, reachable replacement workflow entry points, relevant authorization guidance, and preserved admission/resource-safety outcomes for supported providers and retained compatibility; plugin-source changes pass Docker-isolated Tier-1 validation.
The interface cutover respects existing restart and active-resource safety requirements; removing command registrations does not strand supported active task-native or retained version-1 workflows.

task.implementationPlan:
## Implementation approach

Replace invocation surfaces, not the Episode lifecycle. Reuse the existing preparation, provider, placement, ownership, allocation and handoff primitives. Keep approval/phase reasoning in Markdown; keep only concrete integrity and resource checks in code. No Prime Agent changes or new dependency is required.

1. **Replace command adapters with callable workflow entries.** In `extensions/reviewed-plan.ts`, remove the `plan`, `plan-spec`, `implement-task` and `implement-spec` registrations and their command-only parsers/dispatch aliases. Remove `handoff` registration in `extensions/handoff-chain.ts`. Retain `plan_task`, `plan_spec`, `ralph_handoff` and existing lifecycle tools. Add `implement_task(taskId, host?)` over the existing task implementation prep-chain helper and `implement_spec(location, host?)` over the existing retained implementation prep chain. Use structured arguments and tool-origin steer delivery, not command-only native delivery. Reuse `admitPrepChain`, `admitProviderTaskPrepChain` and `admitWorkflowChain`: preflight both canonical assets, deliver preparation and exactly one canonical follow-up, report admission rather than compaction/readiness/creation completion, and end the calling turn. Preserve first-versus-follow-up transport uncertainty; do not retry or send a second assignment.

2. **Remove invocation-proof approval stores without losing their factual data.** Delete the legacy `ImplementationApproval` map, `TaskImplementationApprovalStore`, grant/consume/skip-next-agent-end logic and expiration hooks used solely to prove a prior command/turn. Remove the corresponding “no matching active /implement-* approval” gates. Do not rename these into tokens, required entry receipts, approved booleans or phase-history proofs. Keep final `create_task_episode` / `create_spec_episode` calls self-contained using the exact selected task/folder. Derive provider, canonical root and Backlog path from existing context and supported native lookup wherever possible; pass only facts that cannot be recovered safely, such as an explicitly selected stable host. Do not add redundant caller-supplied root/path fields, a new binding object or a receipt framework merely to replace the old stores. Preserve actual identity/drift checks and carry necessary selection facts through existing canonical workflow messages without requiring an earlier entry to mint private authority. Inputs cannot redirect the canonical root or supply arbitrary worktree/session/engine identities.

   Reuse `resolveTaskEpisodePlacement` at entry to preserve existing placement/cancellation behavior, carry any selected exact `id:<setup-id>` as operation data, and revalidate that selection at final creation before mutation. Final create must also resolve placement safely when called without a preceding entry. Preserve sole-ready selection, explicit-host/no-silent-fallback behavior, ambiguity/picker cancellation, remote refusal and the existing definitive-Orca-unavailable-only local fallback. Re-resolve current provider/task/root/path and reject genuine binding drift; do not add task-content revision approval locks.

   For retained bundles, deliberately replace the `approvedBundleDigest` dependency on the removed map: capture the current ready bundle digest at the concrete create boundary and use it in the existing capture/promotion/post-copy integrity checks. Keep grandfathered frozen-specification verification and readable meaningful plan checks. Check exact active version-1 replay before requiring the obsolete future folder; source-absent replay must return the same resources with no assignment. Keep `assertConversationPromotionReady` ownership-conflict checks and persisted ownership; those are not invocation-history proofs.

3. **Install discoverable entry skills and align actual loaded policy.** Add thin globally discoverable Markdown skills for `plan`, `plan-spec`, `implement-task`, `implement-spec` and ordinary `handoff`, following the existing initialize-prime-claw skill/tool pattern. Keep entry skills limited to entry guidance and routing through the corresponding tools to the canonical project phase workflows. Keep detailed phase procedures and project-customizable phase policy in those workflows; load them rather than copying complete procedures into global entry skills. Register their sources and targets in `asset-inventory.json` using existing managed delivery classes. Global entry placement keeps them available to active Episode snapshots that intentionally skip project reconciliation. Do not build another installer, copy plugin code into project extensions, or expose lifecycle-only workflows as scanned SKILL.md duplicates.

   Keep the stable inventory IDs and customizable project destinations of current planning/implementation/handoff workflows under `.prime-claw/workflows/`; keep retained `.ralph/skills` fallback where supported. Update source policy, relevant managed builder copies, tool descriptions/guidelines and result messages consistently. Merge intended changes into existing customization instead of resetting overrides or removing old workflow assets. Remove instructions requiring a removed slash command, a separate approval solely because planning ended, or an earlier entry invocation. Planning itself adds no implementation authority; explicit conditional authority may remain valid through preparation/compaction and allow the agent to invoke implementation after the completed plan passes readiness. A planning-only request still stops for review. Bounded delegated selection must bind one exact task before tool invocation; implementation requires existing `In Planning`/`in_planning` after design/planning plus semantic readiness, not dependency readiness alone. Skills clarify material ambiguity or new scope rather than infer authority. Do not encode semantic approval classification or task-selection reasoning in native code.

4. **Prove the preserved outcomes with focused existing coverage.** Extend `tests/reviewed_plan_extension.test.mjs` and `tests/handoff_chain_extension.test.mjs` for tool-origin entries, no custom registrations, meaningful admission results and sole follow-up behavior. Replace tests that require an earlier approval-store invocation with self-contained final-create success and concrete invalid-state/identity/placement/ownership refusal tests. In the existing affected task/Beads/retained Episode suites, retain meaningful-plan/state checks, primary-main/provider publication checks, ownership-before-allocation, exact active legacy replay including absent source, frozen/content integrity, one fixed execute assignment, and partial/uncertain-creation refusal. Exercise the relocated placement/digest facts explicitly so deleting the old stores cannot silently weaken safety. Do not add a new admission state machine or generic test matrix.

   Extend existing initialization/delivery and focused policy tests for discoverable skill installation, unchanged internal workflow IDs, customization preservation and consistent conditional-approval/delegated-selection guidance. Update native discovery probes in `tests/test_reviewed_plan_extension.py` and `tests/test_handoff_chain_extension.py`; update `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` and `tests/test_tier1_driver.py`, which currently require removed commands, to assert their absence and replacement tool/skill discovery while preserving Prime Agent built-ins and `/skill:`. Run affected tests through the existing Docker container bridges (reviewed-plan, handoff, initialization, and changed provider/legacy admission cases), relevant policy/delivery checks, and mandatory `scripts/test-tier1.sh --probe` after every plugin-source change. Record actual results and remaining failures; no host/user-global candidate apply, check or probe.

5. **Update current docs and publish a reviewable candidate.** Update `README.md`, `VISION.md`, relevant Phase 4 text in `LONG_RANGE_PLAN.md`, builder `AGENTS.md`/Backlog guidance, and current prep-chain, handoff-chain, initialization, oversight and retained-bundle docs. Update affected planning, promotion, continuation and initialization user stories plus `docs/user-stories/traceability.md` to match skills/tools, approval policy and actual acceptance evidence. Distinguish removed custom commands from native `/skill:`, internal workflow names and historical references; do not mechanically rewrite historical evidence. Preserve unrelated customizations, ownership/resources and task content. The later implementation Episode publishes its code/tests/docs and bounded native task progress for review; no initial handoff or second execute assignment.

6. **Keep activation separate and safe.** Candidate validation uses existing isolated Docker apply/check/probes only. After a separately authorized merge and primary-main user-global refresh, let affected work quiesce and perform one coordinated full Prime Agent restart. Keep every resource the old generation may read, including retained active plan pairs, until resumed owner/Episode and designated ordinary-session UAT prove the new generation is active and the new skills/tool paths work without custom registrations. Copy success, `/reload` or a fresh probe alone is not cutover proof. Do not migrate/retire retained workflows, delete plans, recreate active Episodes or perform cleanup as part of this interface change. This plan does not itself authorize live deployment or restart.

## Scope limit

Prefer existing provider-native behavior, then concise LLM instructions, then the narrow integrity/transport changes above. No deterministic approval classifier, task reconciliation, iterative-plan controller, phase-history receipt, persistent coordination framework, orchestrator, autonomous backlog loop or speculative hardening. Keep explicit operator authority for product/scope, merge, abandonment and destructive actions. Planning does not authorize implementation; stop for operator review of this saved plan.
